nodes.title: FET Phase
nodes.description: Further Education and Training Phase (Grades 10-12)

nodes.title: Information Technology
nodes.description: Information Technology — Grade 11 — CAPS Curriculum

nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: Information Technology Grade 11 Term 1 covering Solution Development, Systems Technologies, Networks, Computer Management and Social Implications.

nodes.title: Solution Development
nodes.description: Revision of Grade 10 problem solving steps and techniques, nested loops, 1-dimensional arrays, sorting and searching algorithms, parallel arrays, string manipulation, date and time objects.

assessmentStandards: User accounts, logging in, file management
Revision: Using problem solving steps, tools, techniques from grade 10
Revision grade 10 loops
Nested loops (structure and algorithms)
Explain the concept of a 1-dimensional array
Arrays as a data structure (1D)
Loop through items
Basic mathematical operations in an array
Search using the linear and binary search algorithm
Sorting an array (bubble and selection sort)
Parallel arrays
String manipulation using string methods: inserting and deleting characters, determine position of a character, find a character/substring, determine the length of a string
Date and time objects: Changing the date and time, formatting date and time, date calculations, date methods (time to string, date to string, test for leap year)

nodes.title: Systems Technologies
nodes.description: Motherboard components, expansion cards, data flow between components, cache memory, types of OS, programming language compilers and interpreters, processing techniques, virtual memory and virtualisation.

assessmentStandards: Describe the motherboard
Purpose and role of the motherboard
Components as part of the motherboard
Purpose and role of the expansion cards
Flow and transfer of data between components
Purpose and role of cache memory and caching
Memory as part of a computer system
Computer performance
Types of OS's: cost, size, hardware, platform
Programming language compilers, interpreters
Overview of processing techniques
Virtual memory (role and purpose)
Overview of virtualisation

nodes.title: Networks
nodes.description: Physical aspects of a network, communication technologies (Wi-Fi, WiMAX, 5G, LTE), data transmission, network innovation, VoIP, Internet vs intranet vs extranet, VPN, location-based computing.

assessmentStandards: Overview of physical aspects of a network
Communication (Wi-Fi, WiMAX, 5G, LTE)
Data transmission
Overview of network innovation (role and purpose)
Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP)
Internet vs intranet vs extranet
Virtual Private Networks (VPN)
Location-based computing

nodes.title: Computer Management and Social Implications
nodes.description: Safeguarding against threats (physical, hardware, network), remedies, social implications of location-based computing, ethical and legal issues of network use, capabilities and limitations of ICTs.

assessmentStandards: Safeguarding against threats: Safety and security
Threats: Physical, hardware, network
Remedies
Social issues applicable to term 1 content
The social implications of location-based computing
Ethical and legal issues of network use policies and practices
Capabilities and limitations of ICTs

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: Information Technology Grade 11 Term 2 covering Electronic Communication, Solution Development (text files, user-defined methods), Software Engineering Principles, Data and Information Management, Social Implications and PAT.

nodes.title: Electronic Communication
nodes.description: Mobile, wireless and e-communication, use of mobile technology, wireless technologies, protocols and data security.

assessmentStandards: Mobile, wireless, e-communication
Use of mobile technology
Use of wireless technologies
Protocols
Data security

nodes.title: Solution Development - Text Files
nodes.description: Introduction to text files, reading from and writing to text files, exception handling, string handling functions in application exercises, generating text-based reports.

assessmentStandards: What is a text file?
Physical file vs logical file name
Layout of data in a text file: end of line, end of file characters
Text file procedures to read and write
Exception handling
Checking whether file exists
Reading one line at a time
Reading multiple lines
Displaying information from a text file
Use of string handling functions in application exercises
Write to a file using overwrite or append mode
Display the updated text file
Generating a text-based report with correctly formatted data

nodes.title: Software Engineering Principles
nodes.description: What is software development, planning and implementing a solution.

assessmentStandards: What is software development?
Planning and implementing a solution

nodes.title: Data and Information Management
nodes.description: Relationship between data, information, knowledge and decision making, characteristics of quality data, accessing and manipulating data, DBMS, database types, database-related careers.

assessmentStandards: Relationship between data, information, knowledge, and decision making
Characteristics of quality data
Accessing and manipulating data
Grouping data
Qualities of valuable information to build knowledge and make decisions
How to generate information
Describe database management software (DBMS)
Examples of DBMS software
Database types according to usage requirements (size and accessibility)
Overview of database-related careers and roles of people involved

nodes.title: Solution Development - User-Defined Methods
nodes.description: Introduction to user-defined methods, procedures and functions, purpose and types, differentiating between procedures and functions, parameter passing.

assessmentStandards: Consolidate text files and user-defined methods
Introduction to user-defined methods: Purpose and types (functions and procedures)
Differentiate between procedures and functions
User-defined methods with and without parameter passing

nodes.title: Social Implications
nodes.description: Effects of digitalisation, how to protect your online identity.

assessmentStandards: Effects of digitalisation
How to protect your online identity

nodes.title: Term 3
nodes.description: Information Technology Grade 11 Term 3 covering Solution Development (procedures, functions, database programming), Data and Information Management, Social Implications and PAT.

nodes.title: Solution Development - Procedures and Functions
nodes.description: Review user-defined methods, procedures and functions structure, calling statements and method signatures, arguments vs parameters, value parameters, input validation using code constructs.

assessmentStandards: Review user-defined methods with and without parameter passing
Procedures and functions: Structure, calling statement and method signature
Arguments vs parameters
Value parameters only
Using methods in problems
Basic input validation techniques
Input validation using code constructs

nodes.title: Data and Information Management - Database
nodes.description: Creating simple databases, designing tables, maintaining data (insert, add, import, delete, edit), processing, sorting, querying databases, setting up relationships between tables.

assessmentStandards: Create a simple database without relationships
Design the table(s)
Maintain data: insert, add, import, delete, edit
Process, sort, query (generating information from a database)
Set up relationships between tables
Create a query to extract information from a database using a relationship on a maximum of two tables with multiple criteria

nodes.title: Social Implications
nodes.description: Effects of computer and human error, effects of cybercrime.

assessmentStandards: Discuss the effect of computer and human error
Discuss the effect of cybercrime

nodes.title: Solution Development - Database Programming
nodes.description: Using good programming principles, accessing a database through programming language constructs, connecting to a database, multi-form GUI development, database transactions, navigating and modifying datasets, applying algorithms as part of solutions.

assessmentStandards: Using good programming principles and algorithms
Accessing a database through programming language constructs
Set up a connection or connect to a database (single table) by providing path in code statements
Develop a multi-form, multi-screen GUI incorporating simple controls
Use programming language constructs in the execution of various simple database transactions
Access fields and records within a dataset with code constructs and applicable methods
Navigate the records of a dataset
Modify individual fields and records within a dataset with code constructs and applicable methods
Manipulate a dataset object and records with code constructs and apply all changes
Reinforce concepts such as iteration and conditions
Apply simple parameter passing and return values using class methods
Design and develop solutions for specific problems
Apply generic algorithms as part of the solution
Incorporate database transactions managed by methods or events
Devise a specific algorithm where applicable
Motivate the use of a specific algorithm
Reinforce problem-solving steps
Reinforce software engineering principles

nodes.title: Term 4
nodes.description: Information Technology Grade 11 Term 4 covering Internet and WWW, Internet Services, Social Implications, Revision and Final Examination.

nodes.title: Internet and WWW
nodes.description: Evolution of the Internet, software and applications, big data concepts, overview of multimedia as part of Internet technologies.

assessmentStandards: Overview of the evolution of the Internet
Software and applications (definition)
Big data concepts
Overview of multimedia as part of Internet technologies
Media

nodes.title: Internet Services
nodes.description: Overview of internet services technologies, types of websites, supporting technologies and security services, internet-related careers.

assessmentStandards: Overview of internet services technologies
Types of websites (what they offer)
Overview of supporting technologies: Security services (purpose, advantages, and limitations)
Internet-related careers

nodes.title: Social Implications
nodes.description: Social issues applicable to term 4 content, social implications of big data, globalisation and fourth industrial revolution (4IR).

assessmentStandards: Social issues applicable to term 4 content
Discuss the social implications of big data
Describe the influences of globalisation and fourth industrial revolution (4IR)

nodes.title: Revision and PAT Completion
nodes.description: Content using case studies covering all topics, PAT completion including coding, testing and data validation, documentation, finalisation.

assessmentStandards: Content using case studies - all topics
PAT: Coding
PAT: Testing and data validation
PAT: Documentation
PAT: Finalisation
